Discover the Best Places to Visit in Solan, Himachal Pradesh

Solan is nestled in the fertile hills of the Himachal Pradesh, providing a peaceful and lively blend of nature, colonial legacy, sacred places and thrill. If you are planning to visit Solan (either in the short term or the long term), below are the best spots to visit in Solan, the best time to visit and the best way to maximise your stay.

What Makes Solan Special

  • Solan is a place situated between Chandigarh and Shimla. Hence, it has good connectivity.
  • It also possesses a pleasant climate through the whole year with a cool summer, crisp winter and lush monsoon vegetation.
  • Full of culture, temples, forts, monasteries and sanctuaries.

Top Places to Visit in Solan, Himachal Pradesh

Exploring Solan in Himachal Pradesh, one can see a number of attractions that are the combination of history, spirituality, nature and colonial charm. Below is a description of the places that are a must-see in and around the town:

  1. Mohan Shakti National Heritage Park

 This heritage complex is situated in the area about 15 km north of Solan. It is considered one of the most remarkable attractions in Solan. It offers well-designed temples, full-size figures of Vedic rishis, elaborate Hindu designs, and majestic gardens. Its serene surroundings ensure that it is a good recreational area to have a stroll and reflect in peace.

  1. Shoolini Mata Temple

The Shoolini Mata Temple is a sacred temple of the goddess Shoolini and is located right in the middle of Solan town. It is a spiritual centre also as well as a centre of the yearly Shoolini Fair. The fair is attended by thousands of faithfuls and travellers annually. The temple is a great place to visit due to its sacred experience as well as the panoramic visuals of the town.

  1. Majathal Sanctuary

Majathal Sanctuary is a nature and wildlife sanctuary about 26-30 km to the southeast of Solan. The sanctuary, located on rough grounds, carries the endangered Cheer Pheasant and some other bird species as well as wild animals. Its forest paths ensure it is the best place to go on a trekking and photography trip.

  1. Kuthar Fort

It is an 800 years old historical marvel and is located about 34 km away from Solan. The complex of the fort has ancient temples, natural springs, and beautiful gardens that present a rare combination of tradition and nature. The antique nature and serene environment make it a satisfying field visit when you are a history lover.

  1. Menri Monastery

Menri Monastery is one of the oldest Bon monasteries in the world. It is one of the incredible historical and religious sites in the world near Solan. With its colourful buildings and calm atmosphere, it is ideal in case one wants to relax or visit the Tibetan-Bon culture. The monastery is readily available in town and it provides spiritual comfort and breathtaking scenes of the adjacent hills.

Best Time to Visit Solan

Season What to Expect Pros & Cons
Spring (March-May) Pleasant weather, budding green landscape, ideal for treks & outdoor sightseeing. Pro: Clear skies, mild temps. Con: Can get crowded in peak times.
Summer (June-July) Warm but cooler than the plains, lush greenery, waterfalls flow strong. Pro: Escapes the heat of cities. Con: Occasional heavy rains/landslides during monsoon onset.
Autumn (September-November) Crisp air, changing foliage, fewer tourists. Pro: Very scenic, good for photographers. Con: Nights can get cold.
Winter (December-February) Cold, possibly snow in surrounding areas, festive mood, fewer crowds. Pro: Quiet, peaceful, scenic. Con: Some roads or higher routes may be less accessible.

title: Jangeshu Waterfall in Parwanoo: A Hidden Gem Near Chandigarh
excerpt: Jangeshu Waterfall (locally “Jangeshu”) is a serene destination nestled on Old Kasauli Road, near Parwanoo and just ~12 km from Kasauli and 25 km from Kalka. Surrounded by dense Sh…
content:
Jangeshu Waterfall (locally “Jangeshu”) is a serene destination nestled on Old Kasauli Road, near Parwanoo and just ~12 km from Kasauli and 25 km from Kalka. Surrounded by dense Shivalik forest, it’s the perfect escape for nature lovers, peace seekers, and those craving offbeat hill magic.

Why Visit Jangeshu Waterfall?

  • Easy Day-trip from Chandigarh—Just about a 1.5–2 hr scenic drive. The route goes via Panchkula and Kalka to Old Kasauli Road. 
  • Lush Forest Setting—Surrounded by thick green Shivalik foliage. Witness beautiful birdlife and fresh mountain air. 
  • Peaceful Waterfall Experience – Offers meditative ambience away from crowded tourist spots. 
  • Swimming & Picnic Friendly—The Paradise Valley resort area adds a swimming pool & picnic spots adjacent to the falls. 

How to Reach

Route Segment Details
Chandigarh → Panchkula 0–30 min via NH 5
Panchkula → Kalka 20 min through winding Kalka Road
Kalka → Jangeshu Village Another 45–60 min up Old Kasauli Road
Distance ~50 km from Chandigarh, 12 km from Kasauli bus stand  

Which Valley Should You Pick?

Jangeshu features two adjacent valleys with waterfall access:

  • Paradise Valley 
    • Lower part of the waterfall 
    • Includes a swimming pool and sitting platforms 
    • Entry rules restrict solo male groups—couples/families are welcomed  
  • Prem Valley 
    • Upper cascade area 
    • Simpler access, no restrictive rules 
    • Entry ~₹100/person, peaceful sitting zones  

Best Time to Visit

  • 9 AM–5 PM: Optimal safety and natural lighting 
  • Monsoon to Post-Monsoon: (July–October) features the waterfall in full flow
  • Year-round visits are possible, though water levels drop in dry months. 

What to Pack

  • Comfortable shoes (rocks are slippery) 
  • Light snacks and water, though small menus are available at resorts 
  • Swimwear & towels, if you’re planning a dip 
  • Camera for shots of flowing cascades framed by green hills 

Worthy Experiences

  • Swimming Pool at Paradise Valley – Chill by the pool after waterfall walks 
  • Quiet Nature Retreat—Ideal for reflection and tranquility 
  • Photography Spot—Great backdrop for nature portraits & scenic shots 
  • Solo or Group Fun—Few crowds make it easy to enjoy with friends or family 

Visitor Tips

  • Entry Costs: Paradise ~₹100–200/hr depending on activity; Prem ~₹100 entry fee 
  • Group Composition Rules: Paradise restricts solo male groups—plan accordingly 
  • Parking is Limited – Arrive early on weekends/holidays to secure a spot 
  • Watch Your Step—Rocky terrain near the water can be slippery

Where to Stay Nearby?

For an unforgettable stay at the foot of the Shivalik hills, Moksha Himalaya Spa Resort in Parwanoo is unbeatable:

  • Perched at 5,000 ft, just ~8 km from Jangeshu 
  • Features a relaxing spa, infinity pool and luxurious suites. Enjoy the scenic cable-car access 
  • Ideal for unwinding after a day of waterfall exploration 

Final Thoughts

Jangeshu Waterfall delivers an authentic dose of Himalayan peace—from intimate cascades to forest valleys and resort-side pools. Prem Valley is great for a relaxed, flexible visit, while Paradise Valley adds resort comforts if you’re with family or as a couple. Just a quick, refreshing drive from urban hubs, this spot unlocks hidden nature’s embrace in under two hours.

Plan your visit to Jangeshu Waterfall. Book your stay at Moksha Himalaya Spa Resort for the perfect blend of serenity, luxury, and nature.

title: A Guide to the Best Time to Visit Himachal Pradesh
excerpt: Known as the state with the most hill stations and snow-capped mountains in the nation, Himachal Pradesh is a pleasure to visit at any time during the year. Although it is traditio…
content:
Known as the state with the most hill stations and snow-capped mountains in the nation, Himachal Pradesh is a pleasure to visit at any time during the year. Although it is traditionally a summer destination that allows people to escape the heat, Himachal Pradesh offers varying and markedly different experiences depending on when you visit. In this blog, we will explore these differences to find out what is the best month to visit Himachal Pradesh.

The Many Seasons of Himachal Pradesh

Since this northern state is rich with natural beauty and surrounded by tall mountains, the weather conditions and environment here depend on what time of year it is. In the summers, when tourists come here in droves, the state offers a relatively green and bountiful playground of soft grass, leafy trees, colorful flowers and orchards full of sweet fruits. For many people, this is the best time to visit and explore the state.

As the summer draws to a close and fall begins to peak through, you see a stark change in the hillsides, valleys and forests. Many trees and plants begin to shed their leaves and an austere grey landscape emerges from the remnants that gets progressively darker and colder throughout the winter. Many animals go into hibernation and many seasonal businesses that cater to the summer tourists shut down until the next season.

While the winter can be cold and depressing here, it also has its own advantages. Some places in Himachal get snow in the winter, turning the area into a pristine and white wonderland that looks nothing less than a page from a book of fairytales. The snow enables winter sorts such as skiing, snowmobiles and sleighing while different kind of flora and fauna is seen, including thorn bushes, wild berries and migratory birds.

As we know, everything in nature turns perpetually and soon, winter turns to spring. For many, this is a magical and energizing time as life, once in deep slumber begins to awaken with noisy activity and spectacular colors. Flowers and fruits blossom once again and leaves and grass reappear and turn green. In the midst of this renewal, visitors have a chance to see glimpses of life here that are otherwise hidden.

Spring slowly turns to summer as the sun beats down with ever increasing intensity. It may seem odd but the summer sun in hill stations can be quite strong as the thin mountain air does little to dissipate the heat. The beginning of summer is also a glorious time in Himachal as the days are surprisingly hot and the nights are chilly, leading to several different seasons everyday. This is also an exciting time as seasonal businesses and institutions open up.

The Best Month to Visit Himachal Pradesh

Deciding when to visit Himachal Pradesh depends on your individual interests. If you seek only cooler climes, the summer is the best time to visit this state. However, if you are into winter sports and want to experience the state in its original and truest form, try coming here during the winters when it is stripped bare of the tourist entrapments and only the natives remain.

The winters here can be incredibly hard but can also be the most revealing and endearing time to come here. If you stay at a good resort and bundle yourself in warm clothes, the cold weather will not pose any problems and restrictions while the hillsides and landscapes will be dressed up in a different garb that reveals the true fault lines and contours of this earthly paradise.

In the month of December, many hill stations come alive due to their colonial and Christian roots. During this time, you can go on treks, make bonfires and play in the snow. You can also explore tourist attractions easily as there is little or no crowd and everything is easily accessible. The small group of out-of-towners that are present here in the winters are usually seasoned travellers and die-hard explorers who tend to congregate together and are a lot of fun to interact with.

Where to Stay

If you visit Himachal Pradesh in the dead of winters, you should stay at a good resort that is well stocked and appropriately outfitted to fight the cold weather. Amongst all the resorts in this tourist state, perhaps the best and most stylish one is the Moksha Himalayan Resort and Spa. This property is renowned for its spectacular architecture, breathtaking views and an indulgently luxurious property that sits atop a hill.

The rooms and facilities at the Moksha Resort are par excellent and their arrangements are unassailable. This is the perfect resort to use as a base to explore the surrounding areas and interact with natives and die-hard travellers. The resort also has an excellent concierge desk that will help you make travel arrangements, engage in winter sports and find accurate local information. A residency here in the winters is the best way to truly experience the state of Himachal Pradesh.

What is Hurkle Durkling?

Hurkle Durkling is a playful term that refers to the act of slowing down, relaxing, and enjoying life’s little moments. Unlike other mindfulness practices, it doesn’t demand structured meditation or rigid rules. Instead, it encourages you to be present in the moment, whether you’re sitting under a tree, sipping tea, or simply gazing at the horizon.

Himachal Pradesh in November is nothing short of magical. As autumn gives way to winter, the entire region transforms into a stunning landscape of snow-capped peaks, misty valleys, and a serene ambiance that makes it a perfect retreat for travellers seeking tranquillity and adventure. Whether you are looking for a peaceful getaway or an adrenaline-pumping experience, Himachal Pradesh has something for everyone. Here’s why Himachal in November is perfect to visit and enjoy this scenic destination to its fullest.

Perfect Weather for Exploring

November is the onset of winter in Himachal Pradesh, with temperatures ranging from 0°C to 15°C depending on the altitude. The higher regions, like Manali and Shimla, often experience the first snowfall of the season, making the landscape even more picturesque. It’s chilly but not unbearable, allowing visitors to enjoy outdoor activities without the harshness of mid-winter cold.
Tourists can enjoy scenic drives, trekking trails, and peaceful walks through forests covered in autumn hues. Towns like Shimla, Manali, and Dharamshala become less crowded, offering a more relaxed and intimate experience compared to the summer months.

Scenic Beauty

One of the biggest attractions of Himachal Pradesh in November is the potential for witnessing the season’s scenic Beauty. Places like Parwanoo, Kufri, Manali, and Rohtang Pass start receiving snow by mid-November, turning them into wonderlands. 

For those who prefer a more relaxed pace, the pine forests, blue lakes, and clear sky and mountain views make for perfect photography and sightseeing opportunities. If you’re a nature lover or simply want to escape the hustle and bustle of city life, Himachal Pradesh in November is a dream come true.

Fewer Crowds, More Peace

Another great advantage of visiting Himachal Pradesh in November is the absence of large tourist crowds. The summer rush has long gone, and the winter holiday season is yet to begin, making this an ideal time for those seeking solitude. You can roam around the charming hill stations, enjoy local markets, or visit famous landmarks like the Hadimba Temple in Manali or the Jakhoo Temple in Shimla without the usual hustle.

November also provides the perfect atmosphere for introspection and mindfulness, ideal for yoga retreats, meditation, or simply soaking in the peaceful surroundings. If you’re looking to rejuvenate your mind and body, Himachal Pradesh offers a plethora of wellness and spa retreats during this time.

Adventure Sports

Himachal Pradesh is known for its adventure activities, and November is a fantastic time for those looking to indulge in winter sports. As the snow begins to settle in the higher regions, activities such as skiing, snowboarding, and ice skating kick off, particularly in places like Kufri and Solang Valley. Trekkers can also explore lower-altitude trails such as the Triund trek near Dharamshala or the Parashar Lake trek in Mandi. These trails offer a mesmerising view of snow-capped mountains and untouched nature.

If you’re more of an explorer, you can visit scenic spots like Chail, Kasol, and McLeod Ganj, which offer a mix of adventure and culture.

title: Discover Less Crowded Places in Himachal Pradesh
excerpt: Himachal Pradesh, with its stunning landscapes and cool climate, has long been a favourite destination for travellers seeking respite from the heat and hustle of urban life. While…
content:
Himachal Pradesh, with its stunning landscapes and cool climate, has long been a favourite destination for travellers seeking respite from the heat and hustle of urban life. While popular spots like Shimla, Manali, and Dharamshala draw large crowds, there are many lesser-known, tranquil destinations in Himachal that offer a peaceful escape. If you’re looking to avoid the crowds and immerse yourself in the serene beauty of the Himalayas, here are some of the best offbeat places in Himachal Pradesh.

Shoja: The Hidden Gem of the Seraj Valley

Nestled in the Seraj Valley, Shoja is a quaint village that offers unspoiled natural beauty. Surrounded by dense forests, apple orchards, and meadows, Shoja is the perfect destination for those who seek solitude and a connection with nature. The village is also the starting point for several scenic treks, including the trail to Jalori Pass, which offers panoramic views of the Himalayas.

Shoja remains relatively untouched by mass tourism, allowing you to enjoy the crisp mountain air and the peaceful surroundings without the typical tourist rush. Whether you’re wandering through the village or hiking up to the nearby Serolsar Lake, Shoja provides a tranquil retreat where time seems to slow down.

Tirthan Valley: A Riverside Retreat

Tirthan Valley, located in the Kullu district, is another offbeat destination that has slowly been gaining popularity among travellers who prefer quiet, less commercialised spots. The valley is named after the Tirthan River, which flows through it, offering crystal-clear waters and opportunities for fishing, river crossing, and other adventure activities.

The valley is part of the Great Himalayan National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, making it a haven for nature enthusiasts. Whether you’re exploring the park’s rich biodiversity, embarking on a trek to one of the remote villages, or simply relaxing by the riverside, Tirthan Valley promises a refreshing and peaceful experience.

Barot: A Quiet Himalayan Hamlet

Barot, located in the Mandi district, is a picturesque village that offers a blend of natural beauty and tranquilly. This charming hamlet is situated on the banks of the Uhl River, and its serene environment makes it a perfect escape from the chaos of city life. Barot is surrounded by dense forests and offers numerous trekking trails, making it a great destination for adventure seekers as well.

In Barot, you can enjoy a variety of activities such as trout fishing, nature walks, and bird watching. The village is also the starting point for the trek to Bada Bhangal, one of the most remote villages in Himachal Pradesh. Barot’s untouched beauty and peaceful ambiance make it an ideal destination for those looking to disconnect and rejuvenate.

Chitkul: The Last Village on the Indo-Tibetan Border

Chitkul, the last inhabited village on the Indo-Tibetan border, is a hidden gem located in the Kinnaur district. This remote village offers breathtaking views of snow-capped peaks, vast meadows, and the pristine Baspa River. Chitkul’s charm lies in its simplicity and its untouched natural beauty, making it a perfect destination for travellers seeking peace and solitude.

The village is also a gateway to some lesser-known trekking routes, including the trail to Lamkhaga Pass, one of the most challenging treks in the region. Chitkul’s remote location ensures that it remains less crowded, allowing visitors to experience the raw beauty of the Himalayas in a tranquil setting.

Naggar: A Historic and Scenic Escape

Naggar, a small town located near Manali, offers a unique blend of history, culture, and natural beauty. Unlike the bustling town of Manali, Naggar remains relatively quiet and less commercialised. The town is known for the Naggar Castle, a historic structure that has been converted into a heritage hotel. The castle offers stunning views of the surrounding valley and the Beas River.

Naggar is also home to the Nicholas Roerich Art Gallery, dedicated to the famous Russian painter who made Naggar his home. The town’s scenic beauty, combined with its rich cultural heritage, makes it an excellent destination for those looking to explore Himachal’s less crowded, yet culturally rich areas.

Moksha Spa Resort: Your Perfect Stay in Parwanoo

After a day of exploring these serene and less crowded destinations in Himachal Pradesh, unwind at the Moksha Spa Resort in Parwanoo. Nestled amidst the lush greenery of the Shivalik Hills, Moksha Spa Resort offers the perfect blend of luxury and tranquilly. The resort provides spacious rooms with stunning views, world-class spa facilities, and exceptional dining options, making it the ideal base for your Himachal adventure.

Whether you’re looking to relax after a day of exploration or indulge in a rejuvenating spa treatment, Moksha Spa Resort ensures a memorable stay in the heart of nature. Book your stay at Moksha Spa Resort and experience the best of Himachal Pradesh’s serene and unspoiled beauty.

Parwanoo’s strategic location on the border of Himachal Pradesh and Haryana makes it an ideal starting point for journeys into the Himachal hills. Its proximity to major cities like Chandigarh and Delhi makes it easily accessible, attracting tourists who seek a quick escape into the mountains.

Mumbai to Parwanoo (Solitude amidst Nature’s Embrace)

Pro Tip: Regardless of your chosen mode of travel, booking your tickets well in advance, especially during peak tourist season (summer months), is recommended.

Parwanoo: A Tranquil Interlude at Moksha

After your journey from Mumbai, Parwanoo provides a perfect base to unwind and rejuvenate before embarking on your exploration of Himachal. Moksha Resort, nestled amidst the verdant hills of Parwanoo, offers a haven of tranquility. Here’s what awaits you at Moksha:

Parwanoo: Unveiling Local Gems

Kasauli: Colonial Charm amidst the Hills

Kasauli, a charming hill station located around 35 kilometers from Parwanoo, is your next stop. Here’s what Kasauli has in store:

Delhi’s Unique Location

Delhi developed early as a great city because of its unique and enviable location. Sitting on the banks of the Yamuna River, the capital of India is almost equidistant from the great mountains to the north, the arid deserts to the southwest, the fertile plains to the east and several other great cities to the south. It also lies on the main highway of the country, which was once called the Old Grand Trunk Road but is now called National Highway 1.

Depending on where you want to go, you can drive down to many great destinations within a few hours or at most a day of driving and then rest comfortably at your chosen destination by dusk. These road trips can be a lot of fun in their own right but anything further than 300 Kms. can become a bother, especially if you are travelling in a big group or with children.

Also, since Delhi itself is quite congested and polluted, most people want to drive north for a stay in the hills. This allows Delhi residents to breathe in fresh mountain air and enjoy beautiful views of hills, green fields and valleys. The hills are also popular places to go because over the years, many hill stations have developed the right infrastructure required to host large numbers of tourists.

The most famous hill stations of India are further to the north and are also quite congested. This is why Delhiites are constantly on the lookout for good resorts close to the city that can be reached quickly. If you are not limited to only famous hill stations and willing to explore, you can explore the area called Solan in Himachal Pradesh. This region is very close to Delhi and practically next door to Chandigarh, making it the most convenient place for an authentic hill station experience.

The Best Place to Go

Solan has long been known as a beautiful destination perched on a high plate that is surrounded by majestic mountains. Its close proximity to Chandigarh and scenic approach from Delhi is also an added advantage. From here, one can go further north to Kasauli or take a turn towards Shimla. There are also several very interesting villages and tourist spots nearby that are very quaint and charming.

Earlier, a long time ago, there were no good resorts in Solan and therefore it never became as popular as Shimla or Kasauli but nowadays, there have been major improvements in the road leading up to Solan and the infrastructure of the region, allowing visitors to have a fun and luxurious trip to this area. Several new resorts have also opened up here, including the famous Moksha Himalaya Spa Resort.

Where to Stay

The Moksha Resort is easily one of the best resorts in Solan and perhaps in all of north India. It is a swanky and well-designed property perched at the top of a hill with contemporary features and a classy, 7 star look and feel. The resort offers well-appointed rooms that come with all the modern gizmos and gadgets along with a superb restaurant, a heavenly infinity pool looking out towards the hills and an in-house ropeway, which has become a landmark in the region.

Deliites will be especially comfortable at Moksha as it offers the best of Delhi hospitality and efficiency against a backdrop of majestic mountains and rolling green fields. Many of the designers, architects and artists who created this heavenly oasis in the hills are from Delhi and have brought with them the indubitable styling and pomp of the capital.

The resort also offers excellent cuisine that honors the local tradition of cooking but is well versed with global cuisine, especially Italian and Chinese dishes. The restaurants and cafes at the Moksha Spa and Resort serve some delectable dishes during lunch and dinner while the breakfast spread is to die for. Guests who want privacy can also order 24 hours room service that can be enjoyed in the comfort of their own room at the press of a button All things considered, this is one of the best places for tourists to visit around Delhi.

title: Pollution-Free Escapes: Getaway Destinations to Escape Delhi's Pollution
excerpt: Every winter season, the quality of air in Delhi deteriorates sharply and this year is no different. As you may have noticed, Delhi is going through its annual ritual of bad air. T…
content:
Every winter season, the quality of air in Delhi deteriorates sharply and this year is no different. As you may have noticed, Delhi is going through its annual ritual of bad air. This happens every winter due to several reasons. The cold weather stops the convection airflow above the city, which is required to circulate the air and keep it from becoming stale. At the same time, many farmers in nearby Haryana and Punjab burn the stubble from their crops, which releases a dense smoke that settles in Delhi, making it hard to breathe. Luckily, there are many places to visit to avoid Delhi pollution.

As the smog rolls in around the beginning of November, many Delhiites simply up and leave for the hill stations in the North. Just like these hill stations provide sanctuary from the blistering summer heat, they are also the best places to visit to avoid Delhi pollution in the winter and all the health issues it causes. Perched high above the fertile plains of north India, the air at these mountain resorts remains pristine and unspoiled throughout the winter season even as the people in the valleys and plains below struggle to breathe.

Apart from leaving Delhi for a short vacation or retreat, there is nothing else that one can do regarding the smog. Government agencies have been trying different solutions but their impact has been limited. Several years ago, the government started a scheme whereby only odd-numbered cars would be allowed on the road on some days and even-numbered cars on other days, to cut down on car pollution. The government has also laid down strict restrictions for commercial trucks, busses and factories but the problem persists.

 During smog season, the PPM count in Delhi, which measures pollution, reaches critical levels, far above anything seen elsewhere in the world. Doctors and health professionals have declared that this kind of pollution will have dire consequences for residents both in the short and long term. Measures such as air purifiers, humidifiers and masks appear to have a negligible effect, and escape from Delhi is the only option left for most residents.

Where to Go

 To escape the smog of Delhi winters, it is best to head to a hill station that is close by so you can return to the capital whenever the need arises or whenever the air clears up. For this escape, any hill station will do as once you climb even a few thousand feet; the air is perfectly fine. If you go too far to the north and climb too high, the cold weather there may pose its own set of challenges. While Delhi can get a bit chilly in November, some destinations in the Himalayas can get prohibitively cold.

One amazing hill station nearby that you can escape to is Parwanoo in Himachal Pradesh. Only about 6 hours from Delhi and at an elevation of 5500 feet, Parwanoo is one of the best and most convenient places to visit to avoid winter pollution in Delhi. Since it is not as well known as the other hill stations in the region such as Shimla and Kasauli, it is not overcrowded and congested, allowing you a peaceful and comfortable stay. The pristine hills of Parwanoo are a fitting place to enjoy the bracing mountain air and wonderful views of the majestic Himalayan Mountains.

Parwanoo is also a good choice because it is very near Dehradun and Chandigarh. Thus, visitors to Parwanoo are not cut off from civilization and have easy access to most of the goods and services that they are used to in Delhi. With an airport, train station, and big markets nearby, staying in Parwanoo is not that different from being in Delhi. The big difference is that you will not be subjected to the noxious and toxic air that is doing the rounds in the capital city.

Where to Stay

The best place to stay in Himachal Pradesh is the well-known resort and spa called the Moksha Himalaya Spa Resort. This is a lavish 5-star property that has been the gold standard for wellness resorts in the Himalayas for many years now. The property features a stylish infinity pool and breathtaking architecture that will impress even the most ardent travellers and connoisseurs of luxury resorts.

Showcasing the Opulent and Serene Offerings of Moksha

  • Cable Car Ride: Enjoy scenic views in the comfort of a cable car ride.
  • Bonfire Bliss: Embrace cozy evenings with heartwarming bonfires under the stars.
  • Revitalizing Wellness: Rejuvenate at the wellness spa for a holistic relaxation experience.
  • Infinity Indulgence: Delight in the serenity of the infinity pool, overlooking breathtaking vistas.
  • Mindful Practices: Engage in yoga and meditation sessions for inner harmony and peace.
  • Romantic Soirées: Cherish intimate moments with a candlelight dinner experience.
  • Celestial Connections: Discover the universe with stargazing amidst the clear mountain skies.
  • Active Adventures: Engage in outdoor sports – tennis, basketball, badminton, and cricket.
  • Fitness Retreat: Maintain wellness with a fully-equipped gym, tailored for your workouts.

The Moksha Resort is also known for its ropeway, which allows a quick accent to the top and provides breathtaking views of lush green hills and valleys below, endearing people to this iconic location. At the Moksha Resort, you will not only breathe easy but you can also get several treatments at their well-endowed spa that can help you enhance your health and respiration during your stay here.

title: Best Hill Resorts Near Chandigarh: Places to Visit & Stay
excerpt: Chandigarh is one of the best cities in India. Amongst the many advantages of this incredible metropolis is that besides being a union territory and the capital for both Punjab and…
content:
Chandigarh is one of the best cities in India. Amongst the many advantages of this incredible metropolis is that besides being a union territory and the capital for both Punjab and Haryana, it is also ideally located for perusing the best Himalayan Hill Resorts. Due to its unique geography, Chandigarh residents have the luxury of driving up to some incredibly beautiful places that remain a pipe dream for other Indians.

Just 250 Kms. north of Delhi, 230 Kms. southeast of Amritsar and about 50 Kms. north of Ambala, Chandigarh is ideally located at the edge of the northern fertile plains of India and the beginnings of the Shivalik Range of the Himalayas. From here, one can reach the mountains very easily and even plan impromptu trips to the hills whenever the mood strikes.

Although Chandigarh has a pleasant climate throughout the year, the summers can get quite hot and humid. The only respite, as the British found out, was to retreat to the many beautiful hill stations and resort towns in the foothills of the mighty Himalayas, which provide a cool climate as well as a change of pace and scenery.

In this blog, we will explore how best to take advantage of this serendipitous geographic bonus for a rewarding and fun escape from Chandigarh.

About Chandigarh

Chandigarh is the first planned city that India built after independence. Perhaps due to its location and its importance, a lot of time, money and creativity were spent to make this city a model for a prosperous and beautiful post-independence India. With broad streets, organized neighborhoods and designer public spaces, it is a great place to live and to visit.

When India was partitioned, Punjab was divided into east and west Punjab. Unfortunately, the earlier capital of Punjab, Lahore went to Pakistan. To fill the void, India decided to create Chandigarh as a modern and exemplary city to govern Punjab. To do this, no expense was spared and leading international architects were commissioned.

The famous Polish architect Maciej Nowicki and American Planner Albert Mayer created the initial plans for the city. Then, the renowned Swiss-French architect Le Corbusier drew up the master plan, which included the designs for many of the iconic buildings that are still standing. The design by Le Corbusier and its execution was contemporary and clean, giving Chandigarh an international look and feel even today.

Despite its many architectural wonders and tourist attractions, residents of Chandigarh and the many visitors who come here often look for a weekend escape to rejuvenate for a few days. While there are many hill stations to the north, finding a good resort that is cold and close by can be difficult.

Seasoned travellers know that there is little to be gained from visiting a scenic place if there is no good place to stay. An idea getaway location must have an equally good resort that has all the facilities and creature comforts needed for a pleasurable stay in the mountains. A luxury Spa would be an added advantage.

Where to go

One of the best hill resorts near Chandigarh is called Moksha Himalaya Spa Resort, located only an hour and 45 minutes away. This is an elite and fashionable oasis of pampering delights, incredible food and a wellness spa that has become popular with discerning visitors from Delhi and Chandigarh. In fact, Moksha is also on the popular circuit for international travellers who come to India.

With a sprawling and lavish property located at the top of a hill, guests get stunning views of the magnificent mountains and valleys that surround this idyllic location. Not only can they enjoy the cold climate and fresh mountain air, they also have a fully stocked Wellness Center with expert Spa and Salon services.

The Moksha Himalaya Spa Resort also features a stunning infinity pool, a suspended ropeway, pristine forests and impeccable service. It is perfect for a quick getaway, weeklong escape or a longer vacation. It is also ideal for parties and destination weddings as people from Chandigarh and Delhi can attend these gatherings easily.

If you feel like stepping out, there are many places to explore around the Moksha Resort including Kasauli, which is an hour to the north. For a truly exceptional experience, one must visit Moksha at least one and for the people of Chandigarh, there is no excuse not to.

title: Weekend Resorts near Chandigarh: Things to Do & Stay
excerpt: Nothing perks up a week better than ending it with a weekend break to reward yourself. For the residents of Chandigarh, there are many options of beautiful destinations within driv…
content:
Nothing perks up a week better than ending it with a weekend break to reward yourself. For the residents of Chandigarh, there are many options of beautiful destinations within driving distance that provide a stunning change of scenery and a beautiful environment in which to relax and rejuvenate. This winters, take advantage of these places and go on a weekend break that will change your mood and expand your horizons.

One of the best destinations within reach from Chandigarh is the wonderful hill station of Kasauli in Himachal Pradesh. Located only 2 hours away from Chandigarh, Kasauli is the quintessential hill station with colonial architecture, a chilly climate, a buzzing mall street and breathtaking views of majestic mountains. Considered to be one of the best and most developed hill stations in India, this place is ideal for relaxation and exploration.

About Kasauli

Kasauli is a quaint cantonment town built by the British in a strategic location. It has an elevation of almost 6000 ft and is full of colonial era houses and buildings, making it seem like a place from another era that time forgot about. There are many remnants of the raj here including churches, roundabouts, paved walking streets and winding roads reminiscent of England.

Besides its colonial design and construction, there is another reason why Kasauli is such a great place to visit. The town was an army area under the British and this tradition continued on after independence. The Indian army took over the military installations and barracks here and has since contributed hugely towards the upkeep and maintenance of the town. Due to the army presence here, the law and order situation is also very good and everything works perfectly.

Kasauli sees a big influx of tourists every year and has built up the entire infrastructure required to make visitors feel comfortable. From luxury hotels and stylish cafes to interesting shopping experiences and well-maintained monuments, Kasauli is a pleasure to visit in every sense. For a small hill town, the communication and transportation infrastructure is very advanced and many international conferences are held here periodically.

Things to do in Kasauli

The best thing to do in Kasauli is just to relax, take in the views, enjoy the food and wander around. If you are feeling especially energetic and want to engage in some fun activities or check out some of the sites, Kasauli provides plenty to see and do. Here is a short list of the most important experiences you can have here;

Toy Train: A popular activity made famous by movies and popular culture, the Toy Train here is an iconic and memorable experience. It is so popular and important that UNESCO has declared it to be a World Heritage. One can board the train from Dharampur, located about 10 Kms from Kasauli and then ride it to Barog and return. Along the way, there is a 3-minute tunnel that adds excitement to the journey.

Kasauli Tibetan Market: If you are interested in Buddhism and the Tibetan way of life, you will be enamored by the wonderful Tibetan Market in Kasauli. Here, you can buy genuine Tibetan products and handicrafts, which are very good in quality and creativity. You can also buy a lot of foodstuff here such as jams, preserves, jellies etc.

Gurkha Fort: This is an ancient fort built by the famous Gurkha Warriors who were revered for their bravery and resilience. Located in Sabathu, the fort is about 16 Kms away from Parwanoo and surrounded by dense forests. If you like historical forts and are interested in the history of the region, this is a must visit place for you.

Where to stay

The town of Kasauli is quite congested due to the high number of tourists who come here and the relatively narrow roads. Thus, the best place to stay when visiting Kasauli is a good resort outside the city limits. One such resort in Parwanoo is surrounded by nature but is close to Kasauli is the Moksha Resort & Spa. This resort is only 40 minutes away from Kasauli and is the perfect place for a weekend resort.

From Moksha, you can travel up to Kasauli and also visit the many beautiful natural formations in the area. From waterfalls to singing brooks and meandering streams, the drive up to moksha is full of interesting detours that are well worth the time and hassle. By the time you get to the property, you will be in mountain mode.

Once you arrive at Moksha, you will not feel like stepping out. The mesmerizing and impeccable property is a veritable wonderland of interesting activities and facilities that will take you the whole weekend to discover and enjoy. Here, you can swim, enjoy a gourmet meal, get spa services and gaze into infinity at the many look-out spots specially made for this purpose.

If you feel like staying in, Moksha has an extensive room service menu that has everything that you need for a night in with a special someone. The Food is expertly prepared and served and the service is surprisingly quick even though the resort is very spread out. Regardless of the occasion, a weekend trip to Moksha will make you and our guests feel rejuvenated and reborn.

title: Kasauli Hotel Booking at it's Best Deals
excerpt: Kasauli is a wonderful hill station but finding suitable accommodations in tis tiny city is becoming harder and harder. Once an elite destination favored by a discerning crowd, it…
content:
Kasauli is a wonderful hill station but finding suitable accommodations in tis tiny city is becoming harder and harder. Once an elite destination favored by a discerning crowd, it is now overrun with tourists, putting a big strain on all its resources including hotels and resorts. If you thinking of going to Kasauli, you should arrange your hotel bookings ahead of time to ensure a comfortable stay.

Kasauli hotels booking was never easy but in the last few years, its rising popularity has significantly increased the price of hotel rooms and also deteriorated the quality as even sub-par properties are selling out during the peak tourist season. The city has also become more congested and noisy, making it hard to find a peaceful and serene hotel within city limits.

The best option for travellers to Kasauli nowadays is to find a resort that is outside the city but close enough so that you can visit all the landmarks and tourist attractions easily. Some of the new resorts that are opening up in this region are away from the city but within a 50 Km radius, thus giving tourists the best of both worlds.

What to look for in a resort

Depending on your unique needs and preferences, different travellers look for different qualities in a hotel when making their bookings. Some are looking for the most luxurious and lavish properties whereas other are more interested in a prime location that is far away from the hustle and bustle. Still other travelers prefer a hotel that is close to their areas of interest.

Regardless of your specific needs, most people want a dependable and reliable hotel that will not disappoint them and ruin their precious few vacation days. Lets take a look at all the characteristics that are important when you make your hotel bookings:

Location: This is perhaps the most important aspect of any hotel. As discussed, a hotel inside the city will be costlier, smaller and less peaceful than a hotel tucked away in the outskirts and surrounded by lush green forests. Staying at a sweet spot will save you time and money and will also determine what kind of vacation you have. Therefore, you should always check out the hotel location before making your booking.

Swimming Pool:A hotel without a swimming pool or one that has a suspicious pool is not worth staying at. You will not get the “vacation feel” without an appetizing pool where you can sunbathe, swim and order your favorite cocktail. Even if you are not interested in swimming, a hotel with a pool is essential to create the right atmosphere for a fun filled vacation.

Service:Most Indian travellers love good service. They are easily offended when the hotel is not able to cater to their specific needs and feel insulted if the staff is too brusque or curt with them. If you like to be pampered, you should check out the reviews to ensure that you will be well taken care of at the hotel you are considering.

Brand: Branded hotels command a premium price but are worth it because for that extra amount, you are assured that the hotel will maintain a certain minimum standard and there will be no nasty surprises that ruin your day in the sun. Branded hotels have well developed SOPs and systems that can make all the difference between a delightful stay and one that is merely adequate.

Price: Everyone is limited by their budget. You will not enjoy your vacation if you are always worried about the bill. Therefore, you should stay at a hotel that is well within your budget or below it. You can reward yourself later by staying at a top-tier property on the last day of your vacation to end on a sweet note.

Great views: If you are traveling to a hill station, you should stay at a hotel that provides great views of the hills and mountains in the area. This is the best part of staying in the hills and creates the right mood for a characteristic hill station vacation. Good hotels are designed with this in mind and provide great views from the rooms, restaurants and public places.

Good hotels near Kasauli

If you are travelling to Kasauli and are looking for a hotel outside the city, the Moksha Resort is the best option. This is one of the best hotels in Parwanoo that fits all the criteria that we have discussed and also has an amazing spa that can turn your vacation into an elixir of wellness and luxury. The spa services at the Moksha Resort are truly epic and well worth the price.

Besides their spa, the Moksha Resort also has an unbeatable location. It is located about an hour before Kasauli atop a cliff that overlooks the best part of the valley. From almost every part of the resort, you get amazing views of lush green forests and majestic hills hat cocoon you during your stay.

The swimming pool at Moksha is a sight to behold. The stunning infinity pool is designed in a contemporary style and located at the center of the property to give swimmers a commanding view of the area and of the resort. You can order whatever you want by the poolside and also dine al-fresco near the pool.

You can book the Moksha Resort though a number of intermediaries and booking sites but to get the best deal, you should get a quote directly from the hotel. Many hotels give steep discounts on direct bookings and also offer many packages that may suit your needs. If you do not plan to spend a lot of time outside the resort, you should go in for a package that includes all the meals.

Moksha has an amazing fine dining restaurant that offers gourmet multi-cuisine dishes that are cooked and spiced to perfection. If you do not feel like stepping out of your room, you can avail of the in-room dining options that are expertly prepared and elegantly served along with stylish cutlery and everything else that you may need. This is what ideal vacation should feel like.

title: Hill Stations near Delhi within 300 Kms
excerpt: The best part of living in Delhi is its proximity to great hill stations. Most of the famous hill stations in India are located close to Delhi, allowing residents to take off at th…
content:
The best part of living in Delhi is its proximity to great hill stations. Most of the famous hill stations in India are located close to Delhi, allowing residents to take off at the drop of a hat. Whenever the heat or city life becomes unbearable, residents can take a short drive to the hills stations in Himachal Pradesh for a refreshing break and a change of setting that is both invigorating and rejuvenating.

There are many hill stations near Delhi within 300 Kms that are easy to drive to. This is extremely important as most people don’t have the time or budget to take long flights for a few days of luxury. The road trip gets them there fast and is an essential part of the hill station experience. The roads are relatively good and there are many places worth checking out along the way.

Going on a road trip

The best way to travel to hill stations is by road as it gives you the flexibility to leave as and when you want. You can depart your hometown whenever you feel like it instead of being pressurized by flight timings and travel formalities. When you are travelling with family or in a big group, the road trip is even more  fun as it gives you a chance to interact with each other instead of sitting seats apart in a plane or train.

If you decide to go by road, you also have the advantage of having your own vehicle at the destination. This allows you to fully explore the area instead of taking expensive and unreliable cabs everywhere or coordinating with the schedules of public transport. The car also allows you take everything you need with you on the trip instead of being limited by airline regulations.

They say that the journey is more important than the destination and nowhere is this truer than during road trips to the hills. The journey allows you to properly acclimatize yourself and get used to the hills instead of arriving there suddenly by aircraft and then struggling to find your feet. You can also discuss the plan of action on the way and get to know your fellow passengers and the mood they are in.

While it is hard to talk on public transport, you can do as you feel like and say whatever you want in the privacy and comfort of your car. You can blare music and have passionate discussions without having to care about other passengers or authorities. This allows a level of carefree freedom that, to many people, is an essential part of any vacation or break.

Another major advantage of going by road is that you can break up the journey by taking stops as frequently as you like. This allows you to stretch your legs, get adequately hydrated and put less stress on your body as you travel. If you research the route, you are also sure to find some places that are interesting enough to check out, even if you have to take a short detour.

Although driving in the hills is very safe, it is best to err on the side of caution. One should always drive slow, use the rearview mirror, give turn signals and pay attention. Under no circumstances should you drive when sleep deprived or under the influence of alcohol. With a little bit of planning and adequate precaution, travelling by road can be a safe and fulfilling enterprise.

Road trips are fun but it is best not to make them too long. Anything over 300 Kms becomes difficult to cover in one day, especially if you are travelling with children or the elderly. A 300 Km road trip is about the right duration for a fun filled journey without it becoming boring or uncomfortable. A short road trip also allows you to utilize the second half of the day at the destination instead of being fatigued and worn out by the journey. Luckily, there are some great destinations with a 300 Kms radius of Delhi.

Hill Stations Close to Delhi

One of the best hill stations near Delhi is Parwanoo. This is a small town that is closer to Delhi than some of the other bigger and more famous hill stations and also has the added advantage of being at a lower elevation. When going to Parwanoo, you don’t have to worry too much about warm clothing and can decide to take the trip whenever the mood arises.

One of the best resorts in Parwanoo is Moksha Spa Resort that is one of the most luxurious and well-built properties in India. It has a stunning location overlooking the hills and provides a 7 star experience that is worth checking out. Its pristine campus and immaculate rooms are a class apart from most other resorts in the area and provide a hill station experience that is hard to rival.

The resort has a stunning infinity pool that overlooks the valley and a well-designed luxury spa that offers traditional and international massages and treatments. The resort also has a competent gym with the latest fitness equipment and offers many classes and activities for guests like cooking, fitness etc.

The food at the resort is par excellent. Guests get a gourmet breakfast spread that is fit for a king and can also order food and drinks by the poolside. The resort also has in-room dining options that are quick and easy along with a great restaurant and café that is surrounded by large windows for spectacular views that give it that special mountaintop feel.

The location of the resort is also perfect and allows you to make daytrips to Kasauli and other interesting destinations in the area. Within a short distance, you have some interesting adventure sports and also some great waterfalls and picnic spots. If you are looking for a hill station experience that is close to Delhi, convenient and luxurious, Moksha is the place for you.

title: Tranquil Escapes: Discover the Beauty of Hills View Resort
excerpt: The remedy for too much time in the city is a room at a good resort with a mesmerizing view of the hills. There is something about the sight of tall hills covered by green trees th…
content:
The remedy for too much time in the city is a room at a good resort with a mesmerizing view of the hills. There is something about the sight of tall hills covered by green trees that instantly takes one away from earthly hassles and transports us to an elevated state of mind. Perhaps this is why people love to go to hills view resorts in the foothills of the Himalayas to get away from it all.

India has some spectacular mountain ranges and hills in the north that are ideal for a hilly hibernation away from the heat and hassle of the city. Luckily, many of them are undeveloped and relatively unspoiled, giving travellers a close-to-nature experience that is hard to find in other parts of the world. You can get a good view from many of these places but it is hard to find a good resort with the right facilities for a perfect vacation.

Where to go

If you live in Delhi, Chandigarh or one of the cities in North India, all you have to do is travel north by car and soon you will be accosted by the Himalayas. The ground begins to rise slowly and then leads into labyrinthine roads that take you from one hill to the next. While this journey can be slow and hard for some, others enjoy the winding paths that crisscross lush forests, beautiful hills, smooth plateaus and the occasional lake or waterfall.

The Himalayas are a perfect stepwise incline that provides many different types of opportunities for tourists including different elevations, flora and geographic features. Tourists have the choice of staying near a lake or by the river and can also decide how cold they want their destination to be. The northernmost regions of the Himalayas are always frozen as the range is home to some of the tallest peaks in the world including Mr. Everest.

The curve of the Himalayas is also perfectly parallel to the great rivers of the north, making them perfectly placed only a short distance away from the cities that are located on the banks of these rivers. A few hours of driving will get you to the start of the great mountains while another few hours will take you inside these majestic ranges.

The Himalayas also has a well-developed infrastructure as the British started the process of building roads and train tracks to access the interior regions. Although the roads can be a quite narrow and rocky at places and are prone to mudslides and rock fall, one can travel all the way to Ladakh by road if one is so inclined. For most tourists, the drive to their destination is short enough for a weekend break or even an overnight stay.

Most of the famous hill stations in the Himalayas were discovered and developed by the British but the work has continued on since independence. Inspired by the Raj, many Indians have made vacations at hill stations a part of their lifestyle and organize annual, biannual or monthly retreats to these places. The quintessential hills station experience has been widely written about and featured in movies, making it a classic mainstay of life in India.

Most visitors to the mountains do not engage in many activities. While young people are adventurous and like to go for trekking, whitewater rafting, outdoor camping and long walks in the woods, most adults are satisfied with the view and are simply interested in getting some rest and respite in the cool fresh mountain air with great views of hills all around.

The typical vacation in the hills

The standard hill station vacation is 9-14 days long and covers multiple destinations. Families like to get together and embark on their journey to the hills in caravans of 3 or 4 cars, taking with them every item of convenience that they can. They try to leave the city early to avoid the morning traffic and after many stops for food and rest, the families reach their destination in the evening and get settled in by nighttime.

Over the next few days, adults, elderly people, youngsters, and children can enjoy different aspects of the destination while getting together for meals and excursions. The room rate usually includes a buffet breakfast, which forms a suitable forum to discuss the day’s activities and options. With the summer heat dying down and cool monsoon showers erupting everywhere, it is once again time when young couples seek to get away from the city for some alone time. Traditionally, this is the start of the social season, when couples head to the hill stations of India in search of solace and a naturally beautiful environment where they can spend some quality time with their special someone.

Unfortunately, it is becoming harder and harder to find a Romantic Hill Station in India as the old world charm that once percolated through such destinations as Shimla, Mussoorie and Nainital is being replaced by the hum of industrialization. Everywhere you go, there are modern buildings made of steel and glass along with traffic jams and pollution.

Where to go

All the hill stations of India were designed for a small elite and their staff but have now become so popular that thousands of people come here everyday. The narrow roads and quaint teashops can no longer cater to the onslaught of tourists and are hence being replaced by multi-story buildings and wide highways.

This may be good for the economy and the overall development of nation but it bears ill for the budding love that once used to blossom on these hill slopes and mountaintops. What used to be a sweet, endearing and adventurous journey through uncharted territory is now a highly commercialized, garish and noisy trip that few want to take.

Instead, younger couples are now choosing to stage their courtships at luxury resorts that promise a level of sophistication and comfort that makes the whole process more enjoyable and less uncertain. Most luxury hill view resorts nowadays have a refined understanding for the special needs of couples and some have become quite adept at anticipating and filling these needs.

Preset 9-course romantic dinners organized by experts have replaced intimate dining experiences at risky new restaurants. Skillfully guided nature walks around carefully manicured lawns of the resort have replaced treks into the wild. Most luxury resorts also provide a bonfire but instead of looking for dry sticks in the forest, all you have to do is pick up the phone.

In other words, you can still do all the activities that are traditionally a part of the ancient ritual of a romantic trip without any of the danger and risk attached to it. Solan is a beautiful city in Himachal Pradesh that is well worth visiting. It is an ancient settlement that dates back from the time of the Pandavas and has many interesting temples, natural formations, amusement parks, a brewery and even a toy train. This makes it easily accessible by car if you are visiting Himachal Pradesh and an easy city to include in your itinerary if you want to fully experience this beautiful section of the Himalayas.

Things to do in Solan

There is enough to do in Solan to keep you busy for a few days or even a week. Depending on your area of interest, there are a lot of great tourist attractions that you can visit and activities that you can participate in. Let take a look at some of the most popular spots here and what makes them special:

  1. Maa Shoolani Devi Temple: This is one of the most famous and well-known temples in Solan. What better way to start your tour than a visit to this ancient temple and a quick look around to admire its architecture and learn about its genesis? You can also buy assorted knickknacks at shops nearby.
  1. Yung Drung Monastery: This monastery is a major tourist attraction and stores authentic paintings and artifacts made in the Tibetan Style. With an unmistakable aura of peace and enlightenment, it is a great place to pay your respects and learn more about Buddhism and the rich cultural heritage of Solan.
  1. Mall Road: Like most hill stations and hill towns, the Mall Road is the main road here and features some of the best cafes, restaurants, shops, travel services and tourist attractions. Take a stroll down this road to get a good feel of Solan and its people. There is a also a small but interesting children’s park at the Mall Road.
  1. Mohan Meakin Brewery: One of the oldest brewery and distillery in the world, the Mohan Meakin Brewery was set up by the British in 1855. It started as small brewery but grew in size and stature as demand increased. People still visit it to learn about the art of brewing and its fascinating history.
  1. Toy Train: At the Solan Railway Station, you can see and take a ride on the narrow gauge Toy Train that was instrumental for transportation in earlier times and is now a tourist attraction. It has since been recognized by the UN as a heritage site that needs to be preserved.
  2. Mushrooms: Solan is called Mushroom City because the Mushrooms that grow here are famous. When in Solan, try fresh, locally grown mushrooms at one of the restaurants here for a truly divine culinary experience. If you like Solan’s mushrooms, you can buy some to take them home.

For the newcomers to the mountains and hikers club, this trail is the perfect option for you as a starter pack. Nestled at the beautiful foothills of the Himalayas, The Gilbert trail has such a soothing panoramic view that will definitely make you fall in love with nature over and over again.

Come let’s see some dos, don’t and things that you can take with you on this small hike to Gilbert trail.

Do’s

  • Be a responsible explorer : There’s a thin line between being adventurous and inviting danger for you. Be a responsible one and don’t put you and your co travellers in any uninvited problem. Along with this do only what is good for you and the nature for which you are here.
  • Get ready for something unexpected: This 1.5 km of trail will lead you to the beautiful panoramic views which will be completely out of the box.
  • Wear sturdy shoes: Trekking in mountains is not an easy task. Narrow trails can be slippery at times. The Gilbert Trail has a slippery walkway. Wear comfortable and sturdy shoes for your safety.

Don’t

  • Most importantly, don’t litter nature: We all know by now that throwing leftovers, packets is unhealthy for our surroundings. Yet, we see numerous tourists who come to witness the alluring views, but leave the place with packets, empty bottles and what not.
  • Don’t carry too much for just a 1.5 km trail: It’s not a proper trek for which you need many things. It’s just nearly more than a kilometre hike. You can see the next section in the article to know what all you can carry.

  • Avoid touching plants: The beautiful flora and fauna in the hilly areas are way too attractive. But don’t touch any plants as they can cause you serious allergies. Some of them might seem to be fetching, however they may have poison in it.
  • Avoid feeding monkeys: Hills are the home to Monkeys. On your voyage to beautiful spots, you will find these creatures accompanying you. But, do not feed them as they are among the most unpredictable animals.

Things to carry

  • Water bottle
  • One water proof jacket
  • Sunscreen
  • Camera
  • Medicine (if allergic to anything)

Next, when you visit kasauli or surroundings, you have a beautiful hike, which will take you to a paradise. The best time to explore the Gilbert Trail is between April to June and the post monsoon between September to November. Since, in monsoon roads become slippery and it’s risky to trek.
